cards.explanation: The answer is True. The verse says it plainly: "He will be raised and lifted up and highly exalted." That comes right after the promise that the Servant will prosper (Isaiah 52:13). Starting with good news is a smart move, friends, because the next verse gets hard.

The answer is that He was disfigured beyond that of any man. The text says "…His appearance was disfigured beyond that of any man, and His form was marred beyond human likeness…" Many were appalled at Him (Isaiah 52:14). It's a hard picture, friends, and I think it's meant to be.

The kings shut their mouths because they will see what they were never told. The text says "…they will see what they have not been told, and they will understand what they have not heard." The kings go quiet because of what they see and understand (Isaiah 52:15). Picture a room full of important people suddenly out of words.

The answer is False. "Who has believed our message?" doesn't sound like everyone already believes it. I think it sounds more like somebody looking around and wondering who's on board. It's followed by another question: "And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?" (Isaiah 53:1).

The answer is that nothing in His looks drew people in. The text says "He had no stately form or majesty to attract us, no beauty that we should desire Him." He grew up like a tender shoot, like a root out of dry ground (Isaiah 53:2). It's a plain, humble picture, friends.

The answer is faces. The verse says "Like one from whom men hide their faces, He was despised, and we esteemed Him not." He was treated like someone men hide their faces from (Isaiah 53:3). I think that's the heavy part, friends.

The people speaking thought that God had struck Him down. They say, "…we considered Him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted." But the same verse says He "…took up our infirmities and carried our sorrows…" (Isaiah 53:4). They saw one thing, friends, and the verse tells us something deeper.

The answer is Servant. The text says "the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him…" The Servant was pierced and crushed, and the peace comes to the people speaking (Isaiah 53:5). That's the turn in the whole passage, friends.

The answer is True. The verse says "…by His stripes we are healed." The people speaking say it about themselves (Isaiah 53:5). It lands right after the pierced and crushed part, friends, and it's a hopeful line.

The LORD lays it all on the Servant. The text says "…the LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all." Everyone had gone astray, and the weight went onto the Servant (Isaiah 53:6). Notice the word all, friends.

The Servant is compared to a lamb led to the slaughter. The text says, "He was led like a lamb to the slaughter…" It adds that "…as a sheep before her shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth." (Isaiah 53:7). He stays quiet through all of it, friends.

The answer is False. The text says "He was stricken for the transgression of My people." It was their transgression that He was stricken for (Isaiah 53:8). And verse 9 says there was no deceit in His mouth, friends.

The answer is that He did no violence and told no lies. The text says "…although He had done no violence, nor was any deceit in His mouth." He was assigned a grave with the wicked even so (Isaiah 53:9). I think that makes the line hit harder, friends.

The answer is True. The verse says "…when His soul is made a guilt offering, He will see His offspring, He will prolong His days…" It comes right after the heavy line about the LORD's will to crush Him (Isaiah 53:10). The verse doesn't stop at the hard part, friends.

The Servant will justify many and bear their iniquities. The text says "By His knowledge My righteous Servant will justify many, and He will bear their iniquities." It's the same carrying we see earlier in the passage (Isaiah 53:11). He does it for many, friends.

The reason is that He poured out His life unto death. The text says "…because He has poured out His life unto death…" That's the reason He gets a portion with the great (Isaiah 53:12). The reason isn't a win, friends. It's that He poured out His life.

The answer is True. The last words of the passage say "Yet He bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors." He was numbered with them, and He also made intercession for them (Isaiah 53:12). That's a good place to end, friends.
